title: Research: mmap vs io_uring vs read() for asset I/O
description:
Research and benchmark I/O strategies for large asset loading. Compare:

- **mmap** — memory-mapped files, zero-copy to GPU possible (svmesh format). Already in design doc as future parser target.
- **io_uring** — async kernel I/O, batched syscalls, no thread-per-read. Relevant for sequence loading (hundreds of frames). Linux-only.
- **read()** — current approach (read_to_end into Vec<u8>). Simple, portable, but copies everything.
- **Direct I/O** — bypass page cache for large sequential reads.

Questions to answer:
1. At what file size / file count does mmap or io_uring beat plain read()?
2. Can we mmap a GLB and hand slices directly to the GPU (zero-copy end-to-end)?
3. io_uring integration story in Rust — tokio-uring, glommio, or raw? Bevy compatibility?
4. Does the svmesh custom format (from mmap_loader_architecture.md) remain the right target for zero-copy, or can we get there with GLB + mmap?
5. Platform portability — io_uring is Linux 5.1+, mmap is universal but behavior varies. What's the fallback story?

Context: seaview loads 100-1000+ frame sequences, each frame is a mesh file (1-50MB). Throughput matters more than latency for sequence preloading. Single-frame interactive load cares about latency.

Related: docs/research/mmap_loader_architecture.md (svmesh format), parsers/svmesh.rs (future)

title: Epic 3: Bevy Integration
description: Feature-gated Bevy layer. Thin wrappers only. Depends on Bevy 0.18 AssetLoader trait. May need revision if assets-as-entities (#22939) lands. Gate: cargo check -p loadfu --features bevy passes.
notes:
## Tasks

### 3.1 MeshData -> bevy::Mesh conversion (src/bevy/into_mesh.rs)
- impl From<MeshData> for bevy::Mesh (or Into)
- Behind #[cfg(feature = "bevy")]
- Maps positions -> ATTRIBUTE_POSITION
- Maps normals -> ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL (or compute_normals if absent)
- Maps uvs -> ATTRIBUTE_UV_0
- Maps indices -> Indices::U32
- PrimitiveTopology::TriangleList
- RenderAssetUsages::MAIN_WORLD (matches seaview pattern)
- Unit tests

### 3.2 AssetLoader wrappers (src/bevy/asset_loaders.rs)
- StlLoader: impl AssetLoader, delegates to parsers::stl::parse()
- ObjLoader: impl AssetLoader, delegates to parsers::obj::parse()
- GlbLoader: impl AssetLoader, delegates to parsers::glb::parse()
  - Returns Mesh directly — no two-phase Gltf intermediate
  - Multi-mesh: uses load_context labeled sub-assets
- Each reads bytes via Reader, calls pure parser, converts MeshData -> Mesh
- Settings structs with serde

### 3.3 LoadfuPlugin (src/bevy/plugin.rs)
- Registers StlLoader, ObjLoader, GlbLoader
- Replaces seaview's AssetLoadersPlugin
- Simple: just app.register_asset_loader() calls

### 3.4 Integration tests
- Load .stl/.obj/.glb through Bevy asset pipeline
- Verify Handle<Mesh> resolves correctly

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Epic 2 (needs working parsers)

## Risk
- Bevy PR #22939 (assets-as-entities) could change AssetLoader API
- Mitigation: wrappers are thin, easy to adapt
- Consider deferring until Bevy 0.19 API settles if timeline allows

## Gate
cargo check -p loadfu --features bevy passes. Loaders round-trip correctly.

title: Research: VTK format support
description: Research VTK file format support (.vtk legacy, .vtp/.vtu XML). Unstructured grids, multiple cell types, field data. Much more complex than triangle mesh formats — needs its own research pass. See design doc note on scientific formats.
notes:
## Research Complete (2026-02-17)

### Decision: Use vtkio crate behind `vtk` feature flag

VTK is too complex to hand-roll (unlike PLY). vtkio is the only viable Rust crate — 7.5K LOC, handles legacy + XML, MIT/Apache-2.0.

### Scope
- Tier 1: Legacy POLYDATA (.vtk), XML PolyData (.vtp)
- Tier 2: Legacy UNSTRUCTURED_GRID (.vtk), XML UnstructuredGrid (.vtu)
- Skip: structured grids, parallel files, volume cell surface extraction

### Key files
- docs/architecture/vtk_research.md — full research doc
- ref/vtk_samples/ — 10 reference VTK files from vtkio test assets

### Ready for implementation
See vtk_research.md for sub-task breakdown. Estimate: medium epic, similar scope to PLY but vtkio does the heavy parsing.

title: Epic 2: Parsers
description: Pure parsers: &[u8] -> Result<MeshData>. No Bevy types. Each parser is independent. Gate: cargo test -p loadfu — all parsers produce correct MeshData from known inputs.
notes:
## Tasks

### 2.1 STL parser (src/parsers/stl.rs)
- Extract pure logic from ref/asset_loaders/stl_loader.rs
- build_mesh_with_stl_normals -> parse with face normals
- build_mesh_auto_normals -> parse with computed normals
- Input: &[u8], Output: Result<MeshData, StlError>
- Options struct: recompute_normals
- Handles binary and ASCII STL (stl_io auto-detects)
- Unit tests with small synthetic meshes

### 2.2 OBJ parser (src/parsers/obj.rs)
- Extract pure logic from ref/asset_loaders/obj_loader.rs
- build_merged_mesh -> parse merging all objects
- Input: &[u8], Output: Result<MeshData, ObjError>
- Options struct: recompute_normals, triangulate
- Multi-object merge with index offset
- Handles normals, UVs when present
- MTL files ignored (geometry only)
- Unit tests

### 2.3 GLB parser (src/parsers/glb.rs)
- NEW CODE — extend ref/bin/ seed code to full mesh extraction
- Seed: debug_loader.rs::parse_glb_stats, timeline_debug.rs::parse_glb_frame_size
- These already walk gltf::import -> document.meshes() -> primitives -> accessors
- Extend to read actual buffer data (positions, normals, indices) into MeshData
- Returns Vec<MeshData> (multi-mesh support)
- Replaces seaview's two-phase bevy_gltf delegation
- Unit tests

### 2.4 Parser test suite
- Small real mesh files as test fixtures (cube.stl, cube.obj, cube.glb)
- Round-trip validation: known vertex/index counts
- Edge cases: empty mesh, missing normals, ASCII vs binary STL

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Epic 1 (needs MeshData, MeshFormat, error types)

## Gate
cargo test -p loadfu — all parsers produce correct MeshData.

notes:
